subject: botany_2
question_text: What are molecular scissors? Where are they obtained from?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.45, printed question 108. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Revised 2026-09-05: s2_where's second common mistake treated the omission of the enzymes' natural job as an error, although the printed question asks only where they come from and the insider note already offers that detail as an extra, so the entry now names a real mistake about methylation.

insider_note: Two halves and the second is one word: bacteria. Say WHY bacteria have them if you have room.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What they are
steps.margin_note: Name the enzyme class and say the cut is sequence specific.
lines: ENZYMES, which cut DNA at specific locations.
They recognise a particular palindromic sequence
steps.why: They are called scissors because they cut, and because they cut only at one recognised sequence rather than anywhere.
common_mistakes: Saying molecular scissors are ligases. Ligase is the GLUE; restriction enzymes are the scissors.
Saying they cut anywhere. They cut only at SPECIFIC sequences.
steps.memory_tip: Scissors cut, and these ones cut only where told.

steps.label: Where they come from
steps.margin_note: The source, the natural job, and how the bacterium protects itself.
lines: They are usually obtained from BACTERIA.
In the bacterium they are a defence: they cut up
the DNA of any invading bacteriophage.
The bacterium's own DNA is protected by
steps.why: A bacterium needs a way to destroy viral DNA without destroying its own, which is why these enzymes both cut precisely and spare methylated sites.
common_mistakes: Saying they come from plants. They come from BACTERIA.
Saying the bacterium's own DNA is cut as well. Its own DNA is protected by METHYLATION.
steps.memory_tip: A bacterial defence, borrowed as a laboratory tool.
